verdicts.reason: Photo shows the number '42' stenciled in yellow on a dark surface, evoking the forties but not showing the subject of the reading (a person in their forties, reflection, or turning point).

Photo shows a lit candle, a written list/paper, and a botanical sprig on a wooden surface — exactly the ritual props described in the tutorial (three candles, a written list of what you are bringing forward).
Photo shows a candle, a small bowl, dried botanical stems, and a piece of paper with 'Ancestor.' written on it — a flux-schnell generated image that precisely depicts this ritual's materials.
Photo shows properly browned pork sausages in a dark frying pan — the sausage element of bangers and mash is clear, but mash and onion gravy are absent so it is not the complete finished dish.

Photo shows a dark-sauced braised beef stew with carrots and mushrooms over mash in a floral bowl, which is the right class of dish but could be any beef braise rather than specifically Beef and Guinness Stew.
Photo shows sliced beef steak with foie gras and salad garnish on a fine-dining plate — not beef stew with herb dumplings in a pot.
Photo shows a large piece of golden battered fish with chips and curry sauce on a dark plate — a clear beer-battered fish supper, matching the finished dish.
Photo shows a circular braided rag rug (clearly braided and coiled fabric strips) — right craft and technique but the shape is round rather than the oval specified in the tutorial title.
Photo shows skeins of undyed natural white yarn in a bowl beside dyeing equipment — the wool ready for dyeing is present but no bundle-wrapping with plant material or dyed output is shown.

Photo shows a vintage typewriter with a sheet of paper reading 'CANCEL' — directly and unambiguously illustrates the act of cancelling a commitment, which is the exact subject of this activity tutorial.
Photo shows sliced pears on a cutting board with a jar of honey and a honey dipper — shows the pear wood source and honey context but not the carved honey stirrer itself.
Photo shows scissors, pliers, a knife, and a hammer displayed against a wooden carved chair — general repair tools, with no fallen branches or green-wood carving content.
Photo shows three spiral flaky pastries (pain aux raisins / Danish-style swirls) — not a shortcrust crimped cheese and onion pasty.
Photo shows a closed grilled cheese panini sandwich with grill marks on a white plate — contains cheese and bread but is a pressed sandwich rather than open-face toast with grill-bubbled cheddar.
Photo shows roasted/grilled chicken breast pieces with peas on a dark plate — not a chicken and ham pie under puff pastry.
Photo shows chicken pieces being pan-fried in a shallow pan — shows the right main ingredient being cooked but not the finished chicken and leek pie under puff pastry.
Photo shows an Asian-style stir-fry of chicken and mushrooms in a white bowl with spring onions — not a British chicken and mushroom pie under golden puff pastry.
Photo shows a person's stained hands lifting indigo-dyed fabric from a large deep-blue indigo vat — exactly depicts the cold-water indigo vat process.

Photo shows a plate with what appears to be fried meat patties with fried eggs on top, garnished with vegetables — has some hash-like elements (fried meat, eggs) but presented in a tortilla/flatbread style more reminiscent of Mexican food than British corned beef hash.
Photo shows sliced grilled beef steak on a wooden board with tomatoes and a steak knife — no pastry, no crimped edge, nothing resembling a Cornish pasty.
Photo shows marinated chicken pieces grilling on a BBQ rack — not cold poached chicken folded into curried mayonnaise dressing.
Photo shows raw beef mince in a glass bowl — shows the key ingredient but not the finished cottage pie with mash crust baked until golden.
Photo shows a tray of halved hard-boiled eggs with piped bright-yellow yolk filling and chive garnish — unambiguously devilled eggs.

Photo shows sliced dark meat in a rich brown sauce over white mash with vegetable garnish — has the right appearance of offal in a savoury sauce but is too ambiguous to confirm it is specifically lamb kidneys in Worcestershire-mustard sauce.
Photo shows whole raw fish being cut on a stone surface at what appears to be a fish market — shows fish (possibly mackerel family) being prepared but not devilled fillets grilled until charred.
Photo shows a feathery golden-green plant in close-up that resembles goldenrod or a similar Solidago-type plant — shows the dye plant but not the dyeing process or the dyed yarn output.
Photo shows an arrangement of yellow/orange marigold (Tagetes) flowers with red roses — the named dye botanical (marigold petals) is clearly and unambiguously the photograph's subject.

Photo shows blue-dyed fabric with a shibori/tie-dye resist pattern in indigo blue — shows woad/indigo-dyed cloth which is the right output colour and fibre but not the woad leaf extraction vat process itself.
Photo shows skeins of undyed natural white yarn in a bowl — the subject is walnut-hull dyeing which produces brown-dyed wool, and this image shows the opposite: undyed white yarn.
Photo shows stacks of brightly coloured woven textiles (Mexican-style striped blankets/rugs) — woven cloth is the right class but these are not handwoven cloth being wet-finished off a loom.
Photo shows a round salmon and herb frittata/omelette with a slice cut out — not a fish pie with smoked haddock, salmon, and prawns under a mashed-potato crust.
Photo shows a person holding a restaurant guest-check receipt — a bill from a diner, not a body-scan meditation connecting head and gut awareness.

Photo shows a pile of colourful needle-felted wool balls — these are felted wool objects which confirms the felting category, but they are 3D balls not flat felt sheets which is the tutorial's specific subject.
Photo shows Scrabble letter tiles spelling 'FORGIVE' with dried flowers in the background — the word forgiveness is the direct named subject of this affirmation tutorial.

Photo shows a dark herringbone-twill woven jacket/coat folded on a grey surface with a hat — the herringbone fabric pattern matches the tutorial's output but shows a finished garment rather than the weaving process or loom cloth.
Photo shows an extreme close-up of dusky-rose woven fabric with a clear raised hexagonal/honeycomb cell pattern — exactly the characteristic surface texture produced by honeycomb weave.

Photo shows two women hand-processing large amounts of raw fleece/wool outdoors — shows the right class of activity (hand-working raw fleece) but not the specific tool (hand cards) or output (rolags).
Photo shows a person seated with both hands resting gently on their belly/abdomen area — precisely depicts the named physical gesture (hand on belly) that is the tutorial's subject.

Photo shows a geometric-patterned rug on a floor with a trainer/sneaker in frame — the geometric pattern is correct but this appears to be a commercial flatwoven rug rather than a wool-hooked rug being worked.
Photo shows a light-box sign reading 'MAKE YOURSELF AT HOME' — connects to the home theme of the tutorial but is a motivational sign rather than imagery of home habits or domestic life.
Photo shows a rusted industrial metal surface stenciled with 'SAFETY FIRST' — an industrial safety reference with no connection to a body-scan meditation for inner calm.

Photo shows a bowl of clear-broth stew with chunks of lamb, potato, and carrot on a checked cloth alongside crusty bread — exactly matches Irish stew's defining characteristics (clear broth, lamb, potato, carrot).
Photo shows white fish pieces in a creamy white sauce in a shallow bowl — not kedgeree, which should be spiced buttered rice with flaked smoked haddock and hard-boiled eggs.
Photo shows two live young lambs lying in a green field — not the finished Lancashire hotpot dish with its characteristic overlapping-potato golden crust.
Photo shows a lit pillar candle with an envelope and blank note card on a wooden table — exactly the candle-and-letter setup described for this grief-remembrance ritual.

Photo shows sliced dark offal pieces in a rich brown sauce over white mash/grains, with a whole onion and rosemary visible beside — a flux-schnell generated image that closely matches the liver and onions finished dish.

Photo shows Bananagrams letter tiles arranged to spell 'I CANT BREATHE' on a Bananagrams pouch — breath is the subject but the negative phrase and game-tile format is a mismatch for a calming breath-regulation practice.
Photo shows a macramé hammock suspended in a room — macramé knotwork is the right craft class but this is a large hanging hammock, not a knotted plant-holder basket for a pot.
Photo shows a knotted macramé bag/purse hanging under a table alongside other craft materials — macramé knotwork is the right class but this is a bag, not a flat-knotted table runner.

Photo shows a macramé wall hanging with long draping knotted cords above a bed headboard — macramé wall hanging is the right class but this is a cascading waterfall/curtain style rather than the specific semicircular sunrise fan design described.
